items.followUp: Describe any four types of epithelial tissue and state one function or location of each.

rubric.why: Identifies squamous epithelium and gives a characteristic feature.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming squamous epithelium and describing its cells as thin or flat.

rubric.why: Identifies cuboidal epithelium and gives its function.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming cuboidal epithelium and stating that it is involved in secretion.

rubric.why: Identifies columnar epithelium and gives its function.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming columnar epithelium and stating that it helps in absorption.

rubric.why: Identifies ciliated epithelium and describes the role of its cilia.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming ciliated epithelium and stating that its cilia move substances.

modelAnswer: 1. Simple squamous epithelium consists of a single layer of thin, flat cells and allows diffusion; it lines the air sacs of lungs.
2. Cuboidal epithelium consists of cube-shaped cells and is involved in secretion and absorption; it occurs in kidney tubules.
3. Columnar epithelium consists of tall, pillar-like cells and helps in absorption and secretion; it lines much of the digestive tract.
4. Ciliated epithelium has cilia on its free surface; the cilia move substances such as mucus, for example in the respiratory tract.

items.followUp: Explain how temperature and enzyme concentration affect the rate of enzyme action.

rubric.why: Explains that increasing substrate concentration raises the rate until all enzyme active sites are occupied.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the rate increases as substrate concentration increases, and 1 mark for stating that the rate levels off when all active sites are occupied.

rubric.why: Identifies the pH at which enzyme action is fastest.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that each enzyme works fastest at its optimum pH.

rubric.why: States that activity decreases when pH moves away from the optimum.
rubric.description: Effect of pH away from the optimum
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that enzyme activity decreases above or below the optimum pH.

rubric.why: Explains that extreme pH can denature the enzyme or alter its active site.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking extreme pH to denaturation or a changed active site.

modelAnswer: 1. As substrate concentration increases, the rate of enzyme action increases because more substrate molecules collide with enzyme active sites.
2. The rate eventually reaches a maximum and levels off when all enzyme active sites are occupied; adding more substrate then does not increase the rate.
3. Each enzyme works fastest at its optimum pH.
4. Above or below the optimum pH, enzyme activity decreases.
5. At extreme pH, the enzyme may be denatured or its active site may change shape, so the substrate cannot bind effectively.

items.followUp: Define Microbiology and describe one area it studies.

rubric.why: Defines zoology as the branch of biology concerned with animals.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying zoology as the study of animals.

rubric.why: Defines botany as the branch of biology concerned with plants.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying botany as the study of plants.

modelAnswer: 1. Zoology is the branch of biology that studies animals.
2. Botany is the branch of biology that studies plants.

items.followUp: Give one example each of a quantitative and a qualitative observation.

rubric.why: Recognizes that quantitative observations are expressed numerically or by measurement.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that quantitative observations use numbers or measurements.

rubric.why: Recognizes that qualitative observations describe qualities or characteristics.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that qualitative observations describe qualities or characteristics.

modelAnswer: 1. Quantitative observations are expressed as numbers or measurements, for example, a plant is 15 cm tall.
2. Qualitative observations describe qualities or characteristics, for example, a flower is red and fragrant.

items.followUp: What is a pathogen, and how can it cause disease?

rubric.why: Identifies incubation as a time interval between infection and symptoms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the incubation period is the time between infection and symptoms.

rubric.why: Connects the start of the interval to a pathogen entering the body and its end to the appearance of symptoms.
rubric.description: Beginning and end of the period
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying pathogen entry into the body and the later appearance of disease symptoms.

modelAnswer: 1. The incubation period is the time between a pathogen entering the body and the appearance of the signs and symptoms of the disease.
